patch_description: The original program failed validation because it fundamentally broke the required API contract: it returned an empty column_orderings list `[]` instead of valid per-row column orderings, it added an "original_index" column and manipulated/merged/dropped columns (altering shape and cells), it used slow per-row `itertuples`+`getattr` heuristics that don't match the actual objective (character-Trie prefix reuse computed as sum of adjacent LCPs over sorted serialized rows), and its assertions/prints were fragile. The fix is a complete rewrite that: (1) serializes each cell exactly as the evaluator does (`fillna("").astype(str)`), (2) builds up to three cheap candidate row/column orderings — a global frequency-ranked block order using sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)), a recursive conditional partition tree choosing split columns by length-weighted pair repetition within each group, and a length-biased alternative — (3) scores each candidate with the true objective (sort serialized rows, sum adjacent LCPs via C-speed binary search on prefix slices), and (4) returns the best candidate as a DataFrame with identical shape, index, and cell values (object dtype, per-row positional permutation) plus consistent per-row column_orderings. Merged/dependent columns are kept adjacent as blocks without altering any stored values.
